questions.stem: A shape is enlarged by scale factor −2, centre (3, 1). Point A is at (5, 3). What are the coordinates of A'?
questions.explanation: Displacement from centre to A: (5−3, 3−1) = (2, 2). Multiply by −2: (−4, −4). Add to centre: (3−4, 1−4) = (−1, −3). The negative scale factor means the image is on the opposite side of the centre.

questions.stem: A triangle is enlarged by scale factor 1/2, centre of enlargement (0, 0). If vertex B is at (8, −6), what are the coordinates of B'?
questions.explanation: With centre (0, 0), multiply coordinates by 1/2: (8 × 1/2, −6 × 1/2) = (4, −3). A fractional scale factor between 0 and 1 makes the image smaller.

questions.stem: A shape with area 36 cm² is enlarged by scale factor −3. What is the area of the image?
questions.explanation: Area scale factor = (scale factor)² = (−3)² = 9. New area = 36 × 9 = 324 cm². Area is always positive regardless of the sign of the scale factor. Option (b) incorrectly uses 3 instead of 3².

questions.stem: Point P'(1, 4) is the image of P after an enlargement of scale factor −1/3, centre (4, 1). What are the coordinates of P?
questions.explanation: Image displacement from centre: (1−4, 4−1) = (−3, 3). Since image = centre + SF × (original − centre), we have (−3, 3) = (−1/3)(P − centre). So P − centre = (−3, 3) ÷ (−1/3) = (9, −9). Therefore P = (4+9, 1−9) = (13, −8).

questions.stem: A line segment has length 12 cm. After an enlargement with scale factor −1/4, what is the length of the image?
questions.explanation: The length scale factor is |−1/4| = 1/4. New length = 12 × 1/4 = 3 cm. Lengths are always positive; the negative sign only affects direction/position, not size.
